newsitem.title: USA: Chicago futures exchange opens new trading floor.
newsitem.headline: Chicago futures exchange opens new trading floor.

text.p: When the opening bell rang Tuesday morning, the Chicago Board of Trade became the world's biggest futures exchange in terms of size as well as volume.
The $182 million addition of 60,000 square feet gives the exchange a total of 92,000 square feet for agricultural and financial trading -- the largest continuous trading hall in the world.
The exchange already leads the rest of the world in terms of trading volume, with 18,991,093 contracts traded in January.
The new facility, housed in a new building that took two years to build, is more than three times the size of the exchange's former financial futures trading floor.

The cavernous new floor was designed to accommodate 8,000 participants and was outfitted with 876 booths located among eight trading pits. There is room for an entirely new trading floor above, if necessary.
As the first day of trading wore on, floor traders were busy getting used to their new environment -- locating sightlines, working with new brokers and weathering minor technical glitches.
"It's a good thing it's pretty slow in here," one bond options trader said. "If it were busy it would show the cracks a little more."
An exchange spokesman reported a minor problem with a price board, but said it was fixed immediately.
Overall, traders said they were pleased with their new home.
"We're getting acclimated to the floor, but things are pretty good and there's a lot of excitement," said Don Pullen, trading floor bond manager for ED and F Man.
